title: Automated Legacy Library Migration Assistant
business: A specialized software consultancy firm that maintains aging enterprise applications and frequently migrates legacy codebases to modern frameworks.
problem: Engineers spend excessive time manually searching for current documentation and updated syntax for deprecated libraries, leading to fragmented research and inconsistent migration patterns across the team.
solution: The firm integrates the Exa MCP connector into Claude to automate the retrieval of real-time documentation and current code examples. By leveraging the web_search_exa and get_code_context_exa tools, the AI agent can synthesize up-to-date migration paths directly from GitHub repositories and technical documentation sites, ensuring that the generated code aligns with the latest library standards rather than outdated forum posts.
steps: Configure the Exa MCP server endpoint within the Claude environment to enable secure tool access.
Define a system prompt that instructs Claude to prioritize the get_code_context_exa tool when encountering unrecognized legacy function calls.
Execute a targeted search using web_search_exa to identify the most recent official migration guides for the specific library version.
Review the synthesized code context provided by the connector to ensure it matches the project's security and architecture requirements.
outcome: Engineers achieve a more cohesive migration process with reduced context-switching, resulting in higher quality code output and faster resolution of dependency-related blockers.
limitation: The connector relies on external search results which may occasionally include ambiguous or low-quality documentation; users must verify the source URLs provided by the tool to ensure they originate from official project repositories.
